page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r6a.large is a memory-optimized virtual server featuring 2 dedicated vCPUs and 16.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. The instance is powered by an AMD EPYC 7H12 processor running at 2.6 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, utilizing the KVM hypervisor. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks place this instance in the lower tiers for compute and memory throughput. Single-core and multi-core CPU performance tests via stress-ng and PassMark rank in the bottom 10%. Memory bandwidth tests show weak to poor performance, with large block write speeds categorized in the bottom 25% and read speeds in the bottom 10%. Database operations, Redis SET operations, and static web serving throughput also align with the bottom 10% of benchmarked systems.

Given its hardware profile, the ecs.r6a.large offers a cost-efficient entry point for memory-intensive workloads that do not demand high CPU throughput. The dedicated AMD EPYC cores support instruction sets like AVX, AES, and SHA_NI, making it suitable for lightweight caching layers, small-scale database operations, or memory-bound utility tasks where raw processing speed is secondary to RAM capacity.
